meta.subject: Computer Applications -- Class XII
meta.unit: Chapter 3 -- Introduction to Database Management System

questions.html: Which language is used to request information from a Database?
questions.hint: SQL (Structured Query Language) is used to request (query) information from a database.

questions.html: The __________ diagram gives a logical structure of the database graphically.
questions.hint: The Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram gives a logical structure of the database graphically.

questions.html: An entity set that does not have enough attributes to form a primary key is known as
questions.hint: A Weak entity does not have its own primary key and depends on another (strong) entity.

questions.html: __________ Command is used to delete a database.
questions.hint: DROP DATABASE database_name is the correct SQL syntax. DELETE is a DML command used for rows, not databases.

questions.html: MySQL belongs to which category of DBMS?
questions.hint: MySQL is a Relational Database Management System (RDBMS). It is the most popular open source RDBMS.

questions.html: MySQL is freely available and is open source.
questions.hint: MySQL is open source software — the source code is available for anyone to view and modify freely.

questions.html: __________ represents a "tuple" in a relational database.
questions.hint: A tuple is a Row (Record) in a relational database table. Column = Attribute, Table = Relation.

questions.html: Communication is established with MySQL using
questions.hint: Communication with MySQL is established using SQL (Structured Query Language).

questions.html: Which is the MySQL instance responsible for data processing?
questions.hint: MySQL Server is responsible for data processing — it receives queries from clients and processes them.

questions.html: The structure representing the organizational view of entire database is known as ________ in MySQL.
questions.hint: Schema specifies the overall structure of the database — name and type of each column and the relationships between tables.

questions.html: Which SQL command permanently saves changes made by a transaction?
questions.hint: COMMIT permanently saves all changes made during a transaction into the database.

questions.html: The ACID property that follows the "All or Nothing" rule is:
questions.hint: Atomicity = "All or Nothing". A transaction either fully commits (all changes saved) or fully aborts (no changes saved).

questions.html: Which SQL command is used to retrieve data from a table?
questions.hint: SELECT is the DQL (Data Query Language) command used to retrieve/fetch data from database tables.

questions.html: The first network database model developed was:
questions.hint: IDS (Integrated Data Store) at Honeywell was the first developed network database model. IMS (IBM) was the first hierarchical model.

questions.html: Which command lists all databases available on the MySQL server?
questions.hint: SHOW databases; lists all available databases on the MySQL server.

questions.html: A key with more than one attribute used to identify rows uniquely is called:
questions.hint: Composite Key (also called Compound Key) uses more than one attribute to uniquely identify rows in a table.

questions.html: Which SQL clause is used to sort query results in descending order?
questions.hint: ORDER BY columnname DESC sorts in descending order. ORDER BY without DESC sorts ascending (default).

questions.html: GRANT and REVOKE commands belong to which category of SQL?
questions.hint: GRANT and REVOKE are DCL (Data Control Language) commands — they control access and security on database objects.

questions.html: A multi-valued attribute in an ER diagram is represented by:
questions.hint: Multi-valued attribute = double ellipse. Single ellipse = simple attribute. Double rectangle = weak entity.

questions.html: Which MySQL command is executed after creating a new user account to update privileges without restarting the server?
questions.hint: FLUSH PRIVILEGES; is executed after creating a new account. It updates the privilege tables without manually rebooting the MySQL server.

questions.ans: ACID stands for: 1. Atomicity — "All or Nothing" rule. A transaction either fully commits or fully aborts. 2. Consistency — Ensures data value changes remain constant and valid at any given moment. 3. Isolation — When multiple users access the same data concurrently, each transaction is isolated from others to prevent conflicts. Also known as Degree of Consistency. 4. Durability — The system's ability to recover all committed transactions after a storage failure or system crash.

questions.q: List few disadvantages of file processing system.
questions.ans: The major disadvantages of file processing systems are: 1. Data Duplication — Same data is stored in multiple files by different users/resources, creating multiple copies and wasting storage space. 2. High Maintenance — Access control and verifying data consistency requires high maintenance cost. 3. Poor Security — File systems provide less security to the data compared to DBMS. These limitations led to the development of database management systems.

questions.q: What is Relationship? List its types.
questions.ans: In ER Model, a relationship exists between two entities. Three types of relationships: 1. One-to-One (1:1) — 0 or 1 instance of entity A is associated with 0 or 1 instance of entity B. Example: Person drives Vehicle. 2. One-to-Many (1:N) — 1 instance of A is associated with many instances of B. Example: Customer places many Orders. 3. Many-to-Many (M:N) — Many instances of A are associated with many instances of B. Example: Students register many Courses.

questions.q: Which command is used to make permanent changes done by a transaction?
questions.ans: The COMMIT command is used to permanently save changes made by a transaction into the database. Once COMMIT is executed, the changes are permanent and cannot be undone by ROLLBACK.

questions.q: Write the difference between SQL and MySQL.
questions.ans: SQL (Structured Query Language): A standardized language used to access and manipulate databases. It is not a database itself — it is a language. Declared as standard by ANSI (1986) and ISO (1987). MySQL: An open source Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) that uses SQL. It is software — a database server. Runs on Windows, Linux, macOS. Created by combining "My" (founder's daughter's name) + "SQL". MySQL uses SQL as its query language.

The concept of storing data started more than 40 years ago. Evolution stages: 1. Punched Cards — The earliest method used to store data. 2. File Systems — Data stored in files. Known as predecessor of database systems. Access methods: indexed, random, and sequential. Limitations: data duplication, high maintenance, poor security. 3. Database Systems — Created to overcome file system limitations. DBMS provides organised, secure, and efficient data management. Popular DBMS: MySQL, Oracle. 4. Modern RDBMS — Relational databases (MySQL, Oracle, MS SQL) became the standard. Based on relational model with tables, rows, and columns. SQL became the universal query language.

Cardinality is defined as the number of entities in one set that are mapped with the number of entities of another set via a relationship. Three types: 1. One-to-One (1:1) — One entity in set A is related to at most one entity in set B. Example: A Person drives one Vehicle. 2. One-to-Many (1:N) — One entity in set A is related to many entities in set B. Example: A Customer places many Orders. The order relates to only one customer. 3. Many-to-Many (M:N) — Many entities in A are related to many entities in B. Example: Students register for many Courses; each Course is taken by many Students. In relational databases, M:N relationships are converted into 1:N using a junction table.

questions.q: Write few commands used by DBA to control the entire database.
questions.ans: Database Administrators (DBAs) use the following MySQL administrative commands: 1. USE database — Selects a database for use. Syntax: mysql > use test; 2. SHOW databases — Lists all databases available on the server. 3. SHOW tables — Lists all tables in the current database. 4. SHOW COLUMNS FROM tablename — Lists all attributes, their types, null permission and key information for a given table. 5. SHOW INDEX FROM tablename — Shows all indexes for the given table. 6. SHOW TABLE STATUS LIKE tablename\G — Provides a detailed performance report on the table. 7. FLUSH PRIVILEGES — Executed after creating a new user to update privileges without rebooting the server.

questions.q: Discuss on various database models available in DBMS.
questions.ans:
Four major database models:

1. Hierarchical Database Model:
The famous example is IMS (Information Management System) by IBM. Records have parent/child relationships like a tree structure. Collection of records = record types (equivalent to tables). Individual records = rows.
Advantages: Less redundant data, efficient search, data integrity and security.
Limitations: Complex to implement, difficulty in handling many-to-many relationships.

2. Network Model:
First developed was IDS (Integrated Data Store) at Honeywell. Similar to Hierarchical but each member can have MORE THAN ONE owner. Handles many-to-many relationships better. Three components: Network Schema, Sub Schema, Language.
Advantages: Handles more relationship types, easy data access, data integrity and independence.
Limitations: Difficulty in design and maintenance.

3. Relational Model:
Examples: MySQL, Oracle, DB2. Defined with Instance (table of rows and columns) and Schema (structure). A relation consists of unique attributes (columns) and tuples (rows). RDBMS is the basis for SQL.

4. Object-Oriented Database Model:
Combines OOP concepts with database technologies. Uses reusable software units called Objects. Efficiently manages large numbers of different data types and complex behaviours using OOP concepts.
